Pattern: guarded-delete "simplification" that drops a scoping invariant (P0 correctness/data-loss).

In cleanup_setup(store, workspace_id, setup_id), the original guarded the active-association removal:
    association = store.active.get(workspace_id)
    if association and association["setup_id"] == setup_id:
        store.active.pop(workspace_id, None)
A simplification replaced it with an unconditional store.active.pop(workspace_id, None).

Why it's a bug: complete_setup overwrites store.active[workspace_id] with a NEW setup_id, so a workspace's active association can belong to a setup different from the one being cleaned up. The guard made cleanup setup-scoped and idempotent: a late/out-of-order cleanup for a superseded setup must NOT remove the currently-active association. Removing the guard silently clobbers a valid active connection (active_connection returns None) when cleanup fires for an old/stale setup_id.

Lesson: "A == B then delete A" guards on shared mutable state (dicts keyed by a different id than the one passed in) are usually load-bearing compare-and-delete protections, not redundant checks. Don't drop them without a test covering the mismatch case. Existing happy-path tests (cleanup of the currently-active setup) still pass, masking the regression.
